description.value: The study investigated alterations in resting-state regional brain activity and seed-based functional connectivity in patients with congenital right-sided unilateral microtia and severe hearing loss compared with age- and sex-matched normal-hearing controls, and examined associations with clinical variables and the effects of global signal regression.

design.value: A cross-sectional case-control resting-state fMRI study comparing 24 patients with congenital right-sided unilateral microtia and 25 normal-hearing controls after quality-control exclusions. ALFF, fALFF, ReHo and seed-based functional connectivity were compared between groups with and without global signal regression, controlling for age, gender and educational level.

description.value: Hearing level was assessed in a closed field at six frequencies (0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8 kHz).
Cognitive abilities were evaluated using the Mini-Mental State Examination.
Cognitive abilities were evaluated using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment test.
27 patients aged 11–40 years with right-sided congenital unilateral microtia; finally, 24 patients with UM were included.

inclusion_criteria.value: severe HL in the affected ear (>60 dB HL)

exclusion_criteria.value: known neurologic or psychiatric diseases, brain lesions such as white matter hypoplasia, epilepsy, tumors or strokes, and contraindications to MR imaging

medical_condition.value: severe hearing loss in the affected ear

clinical_characteristics.value: Disease duration: 18.6 ± 6.6 years; PTA of affected ear: 75.4 ± 4.8 dB HL.

medication_status.value: Patients who had previously received hearing interventions were excluded.

description.value: 27 age- and sex-matched normal hearing individuals aged 11–35 years; finally, 25 NCs were included.

inclusion_criteria.value: normal hearing thresholds in both ears (<20 dB HL)

exclusion_criteria.value: known neurologic or psychiatric diseases, brain lesions such as white matter hypoplasia, epilepsy, tumors or strokes, and contraindications to MR imaging

medical_condition.value: normal hearing thresholds in both ears (<20 dB HL)

task_description.value: Subjects were instructed to lie still and relax with their eyes closed but not fall asleep and not think of anything.

instructions.value: Lie still and relax with your eyes closed but not fall asleep and not think of anything.

instrument.value: GE750 3.0 T MR scanner with an eight-channel standard quadrature head coil

description.value: Functional images were obtained axially with a gradient echo type echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence.

pulse_sequence_type.value: gradient echo type echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence

description.value: Anatomical images were acquired with a high-resolution T1-weighted gradient-echo sequence.

All rs-fMRI images were processed using SPM12 and SeeCAT. The first 10 time points were deleted, followed by slice-timing and head-motion correction, normalization to the EPI template, resampling to 3-mm isotropic voxels, smoothing with a 4-mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian kernel, nuisance regression, temporal band-pass filtering, and scrubbing.

steps.value: The first 10 time points of the functional imaging were deleted.
Slice-timing and head-motion correction were implemented.
The corrected images were normalized to the EPI template.
Smoothed with a 4-mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian kernel.
White matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals, linear drift and Friston-24 head-motion parameters were removed using a linear regression model.
Volumes with >0.5 mm framewise displacement and adjacent volumes were replaced using linear interpolated data.

description.value: rs-fMRI data were analyzed both with and without global signal regression during preprocessing.

steps.value: Global signal regression uses linear regression to remove the global signal from the time series of each voxel.

model_settings.value: ALFF, fALFF, ReHo and SBFC were compared in the two groups with regression of age, gender and educational level. Gaussian random field corrections used p < 0.001 at the voxel level and p < 0.05 at the cluster level.
Investigated the relationship between brain regions showing group differences and clinical features. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05 with the Bonferroni correction.
